translations.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness to the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran[?]Tophel and Laban and the Encampments and the Place of Gold.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Mount Seir, as far as Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to all the Israelites, according to everything the Lord had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain these laws, saying:
“The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb and said, ‘You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Turn and set out from here, and go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all those who live around it, among the people of the Arabah, in the mountains and the plains, in the south and along the coast of the Canaanites, and to the [?] of Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.

See, I have placed the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that I swore to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.’
And I spoke to you at that time and said, “I cannot bear you alone.”
The Lord our God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the Lord, the God of our fathers, increase you a thousand times beyond your present number and bless you as he promised you.
And how can I alone bear your troubles, your burdens, and your disputes?
Now choose from among yourselves wise, discerning, and understanding men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as rulers over you.
You answered me and said, ‘What you have proposed is good to do.’

I took your tribal chiefs, wise, understanding, and discerning men, and appointed them as leaders over you: commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, commanders of tens, and court clerks for your judges.
At that time I instructed your judges, saying, ‘Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge justly between a man and his brother, and between him and the foreigner living with him.

Do not show partiality in judgment. Judge the small and the great alike, and do not shrink back before anyone, for judgment belongs to God. Bring any case that is too difficult for you to me, and I will hear it.’
At that time I commanded you concerning everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and traveled through all that great and terrifying wilderness that you yourselves saw, along the road to the hill country of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, ‘You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the Lord our God will give you.
See, the Lord our God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of it, as the Lord, the God of our fathers, told you. Do not be afraid or hesitate.’
Then all of you came to me and said, ‘Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us and report to us about the road by which we are to go up there and the cities we are to enter.’
The proposal seemed good to me, and I chose twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They went up into the hill country, reached the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and came down to us. They brought us a report, saying, ‘The land that the Lord our God is going to give us is good.’
But you refused to go up and rebelled against the word of the Lord our God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, ‘Because the Lord hates us, he brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.’

Now where shall we go up? Your brothers have frightened your hearts, saying, “The people are great and numerous and stronger than we are, and the cities are very large and walled up to heaven. We also saw the sons of giants there.”
I said to you, ‘Do not hesitate or be terrified of them.
The Lord our God, who goes before you, will fight against them on your behalf, just as he did for you in the land of the Egyptians before your eyes.
And in this wilderness, which you see, the Lord your God sustained you as someone sustains his own son, along the whole road you traveled until you came to this place.
Yet in this matter you did not believe the Lord your God,
who goes before you on your journey to choose a place for you, leading you by fire at night to show you the road you should travel, and by a cloud during the day.
The Lord heard the sound of your words, and in anger he swore, saying:
“Not one of these men shall see the good land that I swore to give to their fathers,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and I will give him and his sons the land on which he set foot, because he remained faithful to the Lord.”
The Lord was also angry with me because of you, and said, “You too shall not enter there.
But Joshua son of Nun, your attendant, shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he will cause Israel to inherit it.

Your offspring and your sons, whom you said would be taken as plunder, and every young child who today does not know good from evil—they shall enter there. I will give it to them, and they shall inherit it.
But you must turn back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”

You answered me and said, “We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, as the Lord our God commanded us.” Each of you took his weapons of war, and you gathered together and went up into the mountain.
The Lord said to me, “Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not with you, lest you be crushed before your enemies.”
I spoke to you, but you did not listen to me. You transgressed the Lord’s word, disobeyed, and went up into the mountain.
The Amorites who lived on that mountain came out against you and chased you as bees swarm, and they wounded you from Seir as far as Hormah.
You sat and wept before the Lord, but the Lord did not hear your voice or listen to you.
You stayed in Kadesh for many days, as many days as you had previously stayed there.
Then we turned back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, as the Lord had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
The Lord said to me:
“You have gone around this mountain long enough. Now turn northward.
Give the people this command and say: You are now passing through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
Do not provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a single footstep, because I gave Mount Seir to Esau as his allotted possession.
Buy food from them and eat, and buy water from them for a measured amount of silver and drink.

For the Lord our God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. Know how you passed through the great and terrible wilderness. These forty years the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.”
And we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, along the road of the Arabians, from Edom and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and passed along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

The Lord said to me, “Do not be hostile toward the Moabites, and do not provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as an allotted possession, because I gave Seir to the sons of Lot as an inheritance.”
The Emim had formerly lived there, a great, numerous, and powerful people.
As the Anakim are counted among the Rephaim, so these too are like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites had formerly lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau destroyed them and wiped them out from before them, and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land of its inheritance, which the Lord gave them.
Now arise, set out, and cross the Zered Valley.

The time that passed from our departure from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as God had sworn to them.
God’s hand was against them, to wipe them out from the camp until they had perished.
When all the fighting men had died and perished from among the people,
the Lord spoke to me and said:
“Today you are passing by the borders of Moab, in Seir,

and you will come near the descendants of Ammon. Do not act with hostility toward them or provoke them to war, for I will not give you the land of the descendants of Ammon as a possession, because I gave it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.
It is considered a land of the Rephaim, because the Rephaim formerly lived there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a great, numerous, and powerful people, like the Anakim. The Lord destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who took possession of their land and settled in their place,
as he did for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, just as the Lord wiped out the Horites from before them, and they took possession of their land and settled in their place to this day.
As for the Hivites who lived in Hazeroth as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came out of Cappadocia wiped them out and settled in their place.
Now arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have delivered into your hands Sihon, king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land. Begin to take possession of it and provoke him to war.
From this day begin to inspire awe and fear of you in all the nations under heaven, so that those who hear of your name will be troubled, and anguish will seize them before you.”
I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying:
“Let me pass through your land. I will travel along the road and will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell me food for silver, so that I may eat, and sell me water for silver, so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Aroer did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord God will give us.”

But Sihon, king of Heshbon, would not let us pass through his territory, because the Lord our God made his spirit stubborn and hardened his heart, so that he might be delivered into your hands on this day.
The Lord said to me, “See, I have begun to deliver before you Sihon, king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land. Begin to take possession of his land as your inheritance.”
Sihon, king of Heshbon, came out against us, he and his people, to fight at Jahaz.
The Lord our God delivered them into our hands, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
We conquered all the cities at that time and utterly destroyed all his cities, one by one, along with their women and their children, and left none of them alive.
But we took the livestock as plunder, along with the spoil of the cities we captured.

From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the city in the valley, as far as the borders of Gilead, there was no city that escaped us. The Lord our God delivered them all into our hands.
But we did not approach the land of the Ammonites, any of the surrounding areas of the Jabbok Valley, or any of the mountain cities, as the Lord our God had commanded us.
Then we turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Edrei.

The Lord said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him, all his people, and all his land into your hands. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
The Lord our God delivered him into our hands, both Og king of Bashan and all his people, and we struck him down until we had left him no offspring.
We conquered all his cities at that time, and there was no city among them that we did not capture: sixty cities, the whole surrounding district of Argob belonging to King Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fortified, with high walls, gates, and bars, besides the very many unwalled towns of the Perizzites.
We destroyed them as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon. We destroyed every city, one by one, along with the women and children, and left no survivor.
And we took all the livestock and the spoil of the cities as plunder for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the hands of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon as far as Hermon.
The Phoenicians called Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites called it Senir.
All the cities of Mishor, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, were cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For Og king of Bashan alone remained of the Rephaim. His bed was an iron bed, and it is there in the fortress of the Ammonites. Its length was nine cubits and its width four cubits, measured by a giant’s cubit.
We took possession of that land at that time. From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, I gave half the valley of Gilead and its cities to Reuben and Gad.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half-tribe of Manasseh, along with the whole district of Argob and all Bashan, which is reckoned as the land of the Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole district of Argob as far as the borders of the Gergashites and the Maacathites. He named Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, as it is called to this day.
And I gave Gilead to Machir.
To Reuben and Gad I gave the land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, with the boundary in the middle of the valley, as far as the Jabbok Valley, the boundary of the Ammonites.
The Arabah and the Jordan were its boundary, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, from Ashdoth, east of Pisgah.
I commanded you at that time, saying, “The Lord our God has given you this land as your allotted possession. Arm yourselves and cross over ahead of your brothers, the Israelites, all you mighty men.
But your wives, your children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in your cities, which I have given you,

until the Lord our God settles your brothers as he has settled you, so that they too may possess the land that the Lord our God will give them beyond the Jordan. Then you shall return here, each to his own possession, which I have given you.”
At that time I commanded Joshua, saying, “Your own eyes have seen everything that the Lord your God did to those two kings. The Lord will do the same to all the kingdoms against which you advance.
Do not be afraid, for the Lord our God himself will fight for you.”
At that time I pleaded with the Lord God, saying,

“Lord, Lord, you have begun to show your servant your might and your power, your strong hand and your uplifted arm. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do what you have done with your power?
Now let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, the good mountain and Anti-Lebanon.”
But the Lord disregarded me because of you and did not listen to me. The Lord said to me, “Enough for you! Do not speak of this matter again.

Go up to the summit of that hewn mountain and look with your own eyes toward the sea, toward the north, toward the south, and toward the east. See it with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
Command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, for he will cross over ahead of this people of mine, and he will give them as an inheritance the land that you have seen.”
And we stayed in the valleys near Beth-peor.
And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and judgments that I teach you today to carry out, so that you may live and enter and inherit the land that the Lord our God will give you.
Do not add anything to the word that I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Keep the commandments of the Lord our God that I command you.
Your eyes have seen what the Lord did concerning Baal-peor, for the Lord our God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal-peor.
But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today.
See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, as the Lord commanded me, so that you may carry them out in the land that you are entering to inherit.

Keep them and carry them out, for this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations that will hear all these statutes and say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”
For what great nation is there whose God is near them as the Lord our God is whenever we call upon him?
And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as this entire law that I set before you today?

Watch yourself and guard your soul carefully, so that you do not forget all these things that your eyes have seen, and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your children and your children’s children.

On the day when you stood at Horeb before the Lord your God, on the day of the assembly, the Lord said to me, “Gather the people to me, and let them hear my words, through which I will teach them to fear me all the days that they live on the earth, and to teach their children.”
You approached and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain blazed with fire up to heaven, and there were darkness, cloud, and thick mist.
The Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of the words, but you saw no form—only heard the voice.
He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to carry out, the Ten Commandments, and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time he commanded me to teach you statutes and judgments, so that you would carry them out in the land that you are entering to inherit.
And take great care of yourselves, for you saw no form on that day when the Lord spoke to you at Mount Horeb from the midst of the fire.
Do not act wickedly by making for yourselves a carved likeness of any figure, the likeness of a male or a female.
the likeness of any animal on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies beneath heaven,
the likeness of any creeping thing that creeps on the earth, the likeness of any fish in the waters beneath the earth.

And do not look up to heaven and see the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the host of heaven, and be led astray into bowing down to them and worshiping them, which the Lord God has allotted to all the nations beneath heaven.
But God took you in hand and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his own allotted people, as you are this day.
And the Lord was angry with me because of the words spoken by you, and he swore that I would not cross this Jordan and would not enter the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.
And now, here I am, about to die in this land, and I will not cross the Jordan. But you will cross over and inherit the good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the Lord our God, which he made with you, and not to make for yourselves a carved likeness of anything that the Lord your God has forbidden you.
For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

And if you have children and grandchildren, and remain long in the land, and act lawlessly and make a carved likeness of anything, and do evil in the sight of the Lord your God, provoking him to anger,

I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will utterly perish from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to inherit. You will not prolong your days upon it, but will be utterly destroyed.
And the Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will remain few in number among the nations to which the Lord will take you.
And there you will worship foreign gods, made by human hands, gods of wood and stone that neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.
And there you will seek the Lord your God, and you will find him when you seek him with all your heart and with all your soul.
In your distress, when all these things come upon you in the last days, you will return to the Lord your God and listen to his voice.
For he is a merciful God. He will not abandon you or destroy you, nor will he forget the covenant with your fathers that he swore to them.

Ask about the former days that came before you, from the day when God established humankind upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other: has anything like this great thing ever happened, or has any report like this ever been heard?
Has any nation ever heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard it, and lived?

Has God ever been willing to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, through trials, signs, wonders, and war, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with great and awesome sights, according to all that the Lord our God did in Egypt before you, while you yourself watched?
So that you may know that the Lord is God, and there is no other besides him.
From heaven his voice was heard to instruct you, and on earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.
Because he loved your fathers, he chose their descendants after them—you—above all the nations, and he himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to destroy before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as you possess it this very day.
And know today and take to heart that the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below, and there is no other besides him.

And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land that the Lord God will give you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, on the eastern side.
so that anyone who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him previously, may flee there, take refuge in one of those cities, and live.
Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain in the territory of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to Gad; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to Manasseh.
And this is the law that Moses set before the children of Israel.
And these are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that Moses spoke to the children of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt,

beyond the Jordan, in the valley near Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel defeated when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the east,
from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, which is Hermon,
and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan to the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below hewn Ashdoth.
And Moses called all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing this day. Learn them and be careful to carry them out.”
The Lord our God made a covenant with you at Horeb.
The Lord did not make that covenant with your fathers, but with you, all of whom are alive today.
The Lord spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
And at that time I stood between the Lord and you to tell you the Lord’s words, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before my eyes.
And you shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
You shall not bow down to them or worship them, for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me,
and showing mercy to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord your God will not acquit anyone who takes his name in vain.
Be careful to keep the Sabbath day holy, as the Lord your God commanded you.
For six days you shall work and do all your work.

On the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any of your work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreigner within your gates—so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the Lord your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that it may go well with you and you may live long in the land that the Lord your God will give you.
You shall not murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor shall you covet your neighbor’s house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, any of his livestock, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

The Lord spoke these words to your people on the mountain, from the midst of the fire, where there were darkness, cloud, and thick mist, with a loud voice, and he added nothing more. He wrote them on the two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from the midst of the fire, while the mountain was blazing with fire, the leaders of your tribes and your elders approached me and said:

“Look, the Lord God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person can live.
And now let us not die, lest this great fire destroy us. If we go on hearing the voice of the Lord our God again, we will die.
For who among mortal beings has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?”
Go near yourself and hear whatever the Lord our God says. Then speak to us everything that the Lord our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it.
The Lord heard the words you spoke to me, and the Lord said to me, “I have heard the words that this people spoke to you. Everything they said was right.
If only they had such hearts within them, to fear me and keep my commandments every day, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
Now go and tell them, ‘Return to your homes.’

But you stand here beside me, and I will speak to you all the commandments, statutes, and judgments that you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land that I will give them as an inheritance.”
Be careful to do as the Lord your God commanded you, and do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk along the whole path that the Lord our God commanded you, so that he may give you rest and do good to you, and so that you may live long in the land that you will inherit.
These are the commandments, statutes, and judgments that the Lord our God commanded you, to teach you to carry them out in the land that you are entering to inherit,

so that you may fear the Lord our God and keep all his statutes and his commandments that I command you today—you, your children, and your children’s children—all the days of your life, so that you may live long.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to carry them out, so that it may go well with you and you may multiply greatly, as the God of your fathers promised to give you the land flowing with milk and honey. These are the statutes and judgments that Moses commanded the children of Israel in the wilderness when they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
These words that I command you today shall be in your heart and in your soul.
You shall teach them to your children and speak of them when you sit at home, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you rise.
You shall place them as a sign on your hand, and they shall remain fixed before your eyes.
You shall write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land that the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you—with great and beautiful cities that you did not build,
houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, wells dug out that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and you eat and are satisfied,
be careful not to forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians, out of the house of slavery.
You shall fear the Lord your God, serve him alone, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
Do not follow foreign gods and the gods of the nations that are around [?].
For the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God, lest the LORD your God become angry and enraged and destroy you from the face of the earth.
Do not test the LORD your God as you tested him at Testing.
Carefully keep the commandments of the LORD your God, his testimonies and his statutes, which he commanded you.
And do what is good and pleasing before the LORD your God, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to our fathers
to drive out all your enemies before you, just as he said.
And when your son asks you in the future, saying, “What are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that the LORD our God commanded us?”
you shall say to your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and the LORD God brought us out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm.
And the LORD performed great and terrible signs and wonders in the land of the Egyptians, against Pharaoh and his household, before our eyes.
And he brought us out of there so that he might bring us here and give us this land, which he swore to give to our fathers.
And the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, so that it might go well with us all our days and we might remain alive, as we are today.
And we will receive mercy if we take care to observe all these commandments before the LORD our God, just as he commanded us.”

And if the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, and removes great and numerous nations from before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations greater and stronger than you—
and the LORD your God delivers them into your hands, you shall strike them down and utterly destroy them. Do not make a covenant with them or show them mercy.
And do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughter to his son or take his daughter for your son.
Lest he turn your son away from me and he worship foreign gods, and the Lord become fiercely angry with you and destroy you quickly.
Instead, this is what you shall do to them: tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their carved images with fire.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and the LORD your God chose you to be his own people out of all the nations on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the nations that the LORD took pleasure in you and chose you, for you are fewer than all the nations.

Rather, because the LORD loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your fathers, the LORD brought you out with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hands of Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians.
And you shall know that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps his covenant and shows mercy to those who love him and keep his commandments, for a thousand generations.
And he repays those who hate him to their faces, destroying them. He will not delay toward those who hate him, but will repay them to their faces.
And you shall keep the commandments, statutes, and judgments that I command you to observe.
And when you hear all these statutes and keep and observe them, the LORD your God will keep his covenant and show you mercy, as he swore to our fathers.

And he will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the offspring of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain, your wine, and your oil, your herds of cattle and your flocks of sheep, in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.
You shall be blessed above all nations. There shall be no one childless or barren among you, nor among your livestock.

The Lord shall remove every sickness from you, and all the grievous diseases of the Egyptians that you saw and knew. He shall not bring them upon you, but shall bring them upon your enemies and upon all who hate you.
You shall consume all the plunder of the nations that the Lord your God gives you. Your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not worship their gods, for that is a snare to you.
If you say in your heart, “That nation is more numerous than I am; how can I destroy them?”
Do not fear them. Be sure to remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh, to his servants, and to all the Egyptians:

the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and great wonders, the mighty hand and the uplifted arm with which the Lord your God brought you out of there. The Lord our God shall do the same to all the nations whose presence you fear.
The Lord your God shall send hornets among them until those who remain and those who hide from you are destroyed.
Do not be afraid of them, for the Lord your God is in your midst, great and mighty.
The Lord your God shall eliminate those nations before you little by little. You shall not be able to destroy them quickly, lest the land become desolate and wild beasts multiply against you.
The Lord your God shall deliver them into your hands and bring great destruction upon them until he has destroyed them.
He shall deliver their kings into your hands, and you shall erase their names from that place. No one shall stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the carved images of their gods with fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them or take it for yourself, and do not fall into sin through it, for it is abhorrent to the Lord your God.
And you shall not bring the detestable thing into your house and become accursed like it. Rather, you shall utterly detest and abhor such things, for it is accursed.
Be careful to observe every commandment that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and possess the land that the Lord swore to our ancestors.
Remember the whole way along which the Lord led you through the wilderness, to humble you and test you and discover what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.

He afflicted you and made you suffer hunger, and fed you with manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to show you that a person does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell during those forty years.
Know in your heart that, as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God shall discipline you.
Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the Lord your God shall bring you into a good and fertile land, where streams of water and springs from the depths flow through the plains and the mountains:
a land of wheat and barley, of wine-producing vineyards and pomegranate trees, a land of olive trees, oil, and honey;
a land where you shall not eat your bread in poverty and shall lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron and from whose mountains you shall mine copper.
You shall eat and be satisfied, and bless the Lord your God for the good land that he has given you.
Take care lest you forget the Lord your God by failing to keep his commandments, his judgments, and his statutes, which I command you.
Lest, when you eat and are satisfied, and build beautiful houses and live in them,
and your cattle and sheep multiply, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you own multiplies,
Your heart may become proud, and you may forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
and led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, where there were biting snakes and scorpions and thirst, and no water, and brought forth a spring of water for you from solid rock;
who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your ancestors did not know, to humble you and test you and do you good in the end.
Do not say in your heart, “My power and the strength of my hand have made this great wealth for me.”
Instead, remember the Lord your God, for he gives you the strength to acquire wealth, so that he may establish his covenant, which he swore to your ancestors, as it is today.
And if you completely forget the Lord your God and follow foreign gods and serve them and bow down to them, I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will surely perish.
Like the nations that the Lord destroys before you, so you will perish, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Hear, Israel! Today you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of nations greater and stronger than you, and great cities with walls reaching up to heaven,
a great, numerous, and mighty people, the descendants of Anak, whom you yourself know and about whom you have heard, “Who can stand against the descendants of Anak?”

Know today that the Lord your God himself will go before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them, and he will bring them down before you; he will destroy them and make them perish quickly, just as the Lord told you.

Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God consumes them before you, “Because of my righteousness the Lord brought me in to possess this good land.” For it is not because of your righteousness, but because of the wickedness of those nations, that the Lord your God will destroy them before you.

For it is not because of your righteousness or the innocence of your heart that you are entering to possess their land. Rather, because of the lawlessness of those nations, the Lord your God will destroy them before you, and so that he may establish the covenant that the Lord swore to our ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And know today that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God gives you the good land to inherit, for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember, and do not forget, how much you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you acted rebelliously toward the Lord.
At Horeb too you provoked the Lord to anger, and the Lord became angry enough to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
The Lord gave me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God. On them were written all the words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain on the day of the assembly.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

And the Lord said to me, “Get up and go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly. They have already departed from the way you commanded them, and they have made cast images for themselves.”
And the Lord said to me, “I have spoken to you once and twice, and I say: I have seen this people, and indeed they are a stiff-necked people.
Let me destroy them, and I will blot out their name from under heaven and make you into a great nation, stronger and more numerous than this one.”
Then I turned and came down from the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire, and the two tablets were in my two hands.
And when I saw that you had sinned before the Lord our God, made cast idols for yourselves, and strayed from the path that the Lord had commanded,
I took the two tablets from my hands and shattered them before your eyes.

And I pleaded before the Lord a second time, as I had the first time, for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all your sins, which you committed by doing evil before the Lord our God and provoking him to anger.
I was terrified because of the anger and fury with which the Lord was angry with you, intending to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me at that time.
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron and intended to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron too at that time.

And I took your sin, the calf you had made, and burned it with fire. I broke it up and crushed it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw the dust into the stream that flowed down from the mountain.
And at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked the Lord your God to anger.

And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, “Go up and take possession of the land that I am going to give you,” you rebelled against the word of the Lord your God. You did not believe him or listen to the Lord’s voice.
For you were rebellious toward the Lord from the day he became known to you.
And I pleaded before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, during which they pleaded, because the Lord had said he would destroy you.

And I stood in prayer before the Lord and said, “Lord, Lord, King of gods, do not destroy your people and your allotted possession, whom you redeemed by your great power, whom you brought out of Egypt by your great power, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm.”
Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness and their sins.

Otherwise, the inhabitants of the land from which you brought us out may say, “Because the Lord could not bring them into the land he promised them, and because the Lord hated them, he brought them out to slaughter them in the wilderness.”
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your uplifted arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, “Cut two stone tablets for yourself like the first ones, and come up the mountain. Make a wooden ark for yourself.
I will write on the tablets the same words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered, and you shall put them inside the ark.”
And I made an ark of wood that does not decay, and I cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
And he wrote on the two tablets, as in the first writing, the ten commandments that the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire. And the Lord gave them to me.
And I turned and came down from the mountain, and I put the tablets inside the ark. They remained there, as the Lord had commanded me.
And the Israelites journeyed from Beeroth of the sons of Jakim to Sadai. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they journeyed to Gadgad, and from Gadgad to Etaka, a land of streams of water.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to stand before the Lord to serve him, and to offer prayers in his name, as they do to this day.
Therefore the Levites have no share or inheritance among their brothers, for the Lord himself is their portion and inheritance, as he told them.
And I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me at that time and did not wish to destroy you.
And the Lord said to me, “Go, journey ahead of this people, so that they may enter and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.”
And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you except to fear the Lord your God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul?
And to keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his laws, which I command you today, so that things may go well for you.
Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens, the earth and everything in them.
But the Lord first took delight in your ancestors and loved them, and he chose their descendants after them—you—above all the nations, as is the case today.
Circumcise your hardened hearts, and no longer stiffen your necks.
For the Lord our God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
He gives justice to the newcomer, the orphan, and the widow, and loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
And love the foreigner, for you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the Lord your God, serve him, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
For he is your glory and your God, who has done for you the great and glorious things that your eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt as seventy people, and now, look, the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.
You shall love the Lord your God and keep his observances, his statutes, his commandments, and his judgments all the days of your life.
And recognize today that this is not about your children, who have neither known nor seen the discipline of the Lord your God, his great deeds, his mighty hand, and his outstretched arm,
his signs and the deeds he performed in Egypt against Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and against all his land,

and what he did to the Egyptian army, their chariots, and their horses: how he made the waters of the Red Sea surge over their faces as they pursued us. The Lord destroyed them, and they remain destroyed to this day.
And what he did for you there in the wilderness until you came to this place,

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and all their possessions with them, from the midst of all Israel.
For your own eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord that he has done for you up to this day.
And keep all his commandments that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and possess the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess,
so that you may live long in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give them and their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are about to enter and possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where people sow seed and water it with their feet like a vegetable garden.
Rather, the land you are about to enter and possess is a land of mountains and plains, which drinks water from the rain of heaven,
a land that the Lord your God cares for. The eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
And if you faithfully obey all his commandments that I command you today, loving the Lord your God and serving him with all your heart and with all your soul,
he will give rain to your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
And he will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
Watch yourselves, lest your hearts grow careless and you turn aside, serve foreign gods, and bow down to them.

And the Lord will become angry with you and shut up the heavens, so that there will be no rain and the land will not yield its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that the Lord gave you.
And you shall place these words in your hearts and souls, and bind them as a sign on your hands, and they shall remain fixed before your eyes.
And you shall teach your children to speak of them when sitting in the house, when traveling along the road, when lying down, and when rising.
And you shall write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
So that your days and the days of your children may be many in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give you, as long as the heavens are above the earth.
And if you diligently obey all these commandments that I command you today to carry out—to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to hold fast to him—
the Lord will drive out all those nations before you, and you shall dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourselves.
Every place where your feet tread shall be yours. From the wilderness as far as the [?] of Lebanon, and from the great river, the River Euphrates, as far as the western sea, shall be your boundaries.
And no one will stand against you. The Lord your God will put dread and fear of you upon the whole land where you tread, as the Lord said to you.
And see, today I set before you a blessing and a curse:
a blessing if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today;
and a curse if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today, but stray from the way that I commanded you, going to worship foreign gods whom you do not know.
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess, you shall pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not beyond the Jordan, behind the road toward the west, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell toward the west, near Gilgal, beside the lofty oak?
And you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the Lord God will give you as an inheritance for all time. You shall possess it and live in it.
And you shall take care to carry out all his statutes and these judgments that I set before you today.

And these are the statutes and judgments that you shall take care to carry out in the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, will give you as an inheritance, all the days that you live on the earth.
You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations you will dispossess worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
And you shall tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, burn their sacred groves with fire, break apart the carved images of their gods, and erase their names from that place.
And you shall not do the same to the Lord your God.
Instead, you shall seek the place that the Lord your God will choose in one of your tribes to place his name and have it invoked there, and you shall go there.
And you shall bring your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your produce, your vowed offerings, your freewill offerings, your thank offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep.
And you shall eat before the Lord your God, and you and your households shall rejoice in everything to which you put your hands, as the Lord your God has blessed you.
Do not do everything that we are not doing here today, each person doing what is pleasing in his own eyes.
For to this day you have not reached the rest and the inheritance that the Lord our God will give you.
You will cross the Jordan and live in the land that the Lord our God will give you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies who are around [?], and you will live securely.

There will be a place that the Lord our God chooses for his name to be called upon it. There you shall bring everything that I command you today: your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the produce of your hands, your gifts, and all your choicest offerings that you vow to your God.
You shall rejoice before the Lord our God—you, your sons, your daughters, your male servants, your female servants, and the Levite within your gates, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
Take care not to offer your burnt offerings in every place you see.
Instead, offer your burnt offerings in the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself in one of your towns. There you shall do everything that I command you today.

You may slaughter animals and eat meat whenever you wish, according to the blessing the Lord your God has given you, in all your towns. Both the unclean and the clean among you may eat it together, as they would gazelle or deer.
But do not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water.

Do not dare to eat within your towns the tithes of your grain, wine, and oil, the firstborn of your cattle and sheep, any of the offerings you vow, your thanksgiving offerings, or the produce of your hands.

Instead, you shall eat these before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord God chooses for himself—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the foreigner within your towns. You shall rejoice before the Lord your God in everything to which you put your hand.
Take care not to abandon the Levite all your days, as long as you live on the earth.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he promised you, and you say, “I will eat meat,” because you desire to eat meat, you may eat meat according to all your desire.

If the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called upon it is too far from you, you may slaughter some of the cattle and sheep that God gives you, as I commanded you, and eat within your towns according to your desire.
You shall eat it just as a gazelle or a deer is eaten. Both the unclean and the clean among you may eat it alike.
Take care not to eat the blood, because its blood is its life.
Do not eat the life with the meat; pour it out on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
But take the holy offerings that you have and the offerings that you vow, and come to the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself, for his name to be called upon it.

You shall offer your burnt offerings, putting the meat on the altar of the Lord your God. You shall pour out the blood of the sacrifices at the base of the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the meat.
Be careful, listen, and carry out all the words that I command you, so that it may go well with you and your children forever, and do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
When the Lord your God destroys before you the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you take possession of their land and live in it,

Take care not to seek to follow them after they have been destroyed from before you. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, “How do these nations serve their gods, so that I too may do the same for the Lord?”
Do not treat the Lord your God in the same way, for they did for their gods the detestable things that the Lord hates: they burn their sons and daughters in fire for their gods.
Be careful to do everything that I command you today. Do not add to it or take anything away from it.
If a prophet or an interpreter of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or wonder he spoke to you about comes to pass, and he says, “Let us go and worship foreign gods whom you do not know,”
do not listen to the words of that prophet or interpreter of dreams, for the Lord God is testing you to know whether you love the Lord our God with all your heart and all your soul.
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, listen to his voice, and hold fast to him.

That prophet or interpreter of dreams must die, because he spoke to make you rebel against the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the land of slavery, to turn you away from the path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow. You must remove the evil from among you.

If your brother, whether through your father or your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife of your embrace, or a friend who is like your own self secretly urges you, saying, “Let us go and worship foreign gods whom neither you nor your fathers have known,”
from among the gods of the nations around you, whether near you or far away, from one end of the earth to the other,
do not agree with him or listen to him. Do not look on him with pity, have compassion on him, or conceal him.
You must report him. Your hand must be the first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
Stone him with stones so that he dies, because he sought to make you rebel against the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
All Israel will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer do such an evil thing among you.
If you hear it said in one of the cities that the Lord your God gives you to live in,
“Lawless men have gone out from among us and led all the inhabitants of their city into rebellion, saying, ‘Let us go and worship foreign gods whom you do not know,’”
then investigate, inquire, and make a thorough search. If the report is indeed true and confirmed, and this detestable thing has happened among you,
you must slaughter all the inhabitants of that land with the sword. You must devote it and everything in it to destruction, and put their livestock to the sword.
Gather all its plunder at its exits, and burn the city and all its spoil together with fire before the Lord your God. It must remain a ruin forever and never be rebuilt.

Nothing devoted to destruction must cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn from his fierce anger, grant you mercy, have compassion on you, and multiply you, just as the Lord swore to your fathers,
if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his commandments that I command you today, and doing what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
For you are children of the Lord your God. Do not cut yourselves or strike your forehead for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God has chosen you to be his own people out of all the nations on the face of the earth.
Do not eat anything detestable.
These are the animals you may eat: cattle, sheep from the flocks, and male goats.
The deer, the gazelle, the buffalo, the wild goat, the antelope, the oryx, and the giraffe.
You may eat any animal that has split hooves divided into two parts and chews the cud.

But you must not eat those that chew the cud but do not have split hooves divided into two parts: the camel, the hare, and the rabbit. They chew the cud but do not have split hooves; they are unclean for you.
And the pig, because it has split hooves divided into two parts but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
These are what you may eat of everything that lives in the waters: you may eat anything that has fins and scales.
But you must not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; they are unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
These are the ones you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the sea eagle;
the kite, the vulture, and anything like them;
the raven and anything like it;
the ostrich, the owl, the jay, and the stork;
the [?], the kestrel, and the swan;
the nightingale, the crow, and the pelican;
the plover and anything like them, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every creeping winged creature shall be unclean for you, and you must not eat any of them.
You may eat any clean flying creature.

You must not eat anything that has died on its own. You may give it to the resident stranger in your towns, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You must not cook a lamb in its mother's milk.
You must set aside a tenth of all the produce of your seed, the crops of your fields, year after year.

You shall eat it before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God chooses to put his name upon. There you shall present the tithes of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.
But if the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place that the Lord your God chooses to put his name there is far from you, because the Lord your God has blessed you,
you shall sell it for silver, take the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses.
You shall spend the silver on whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you desire. You shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your son.
You must not neglect the Levite in your towns, for he has no share or inheritance with you.
At the end of three years, you shall bring out the entire tithe of your produce from that year and store it in your towns.

And the Levite shall come, because he has no share or inheritance with you, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow in your towns shall eat and be satisfied, so that the Lord your God may bless you in every work you do.
Every seventh year you shall grant a release from debts.

And this shall be the rule for the release: you shall cancel every debt that your neighbor owes you, and you shall not demand repayment from your neighbor or your brother, because a release has been proclaimed for the Lord your God.
You may demand from a foreigner whatever he owes you, but you shall release your brother from his debts to you.
There shall be no one in need among you, for the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess.
And if you listen carefully to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and carrying out all the commandments that I command you today,
For the Lord your God has blessed you as he promised you. You shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. You shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

And if there is a needy person among you, one of your brothers in any of your towns in the land that the Lord your God gives you, you shall not turn your heart away or close your hand to your needy brother.
Instead, you shall open your hand generously to him and lend him as much as he asks for in his need.

Be on your guard, lest a secret lawless thought arise in your heart and you say, “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” and you look with ill will on your needy brother and give him nothing. Then he may cry out against you to the Lord, and these will be great sins on your part.

Instead, you shall give generously to him and lend him as much as he needs. Do not be grieved in your heart after giving to him, because for this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.
For the needy will never cease to be in the land. Therefore I command this and say: You shall open your hand wide to your brother, to the poor and afflicted in your land.
And if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, that person shall serve you for six years, and in the seventh year you shall set that person free from you.
And when you set that person free, you shall not send that person away empty-handed.
Instead, you shall provide generously from your flock, your grain, and your winepress. You shall give to that person according to how the Lord your God has blessed you.
And you shall remember that you too were a slave in the land of the Egyptians, and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. Therefore I command you to do these things.
But if he says to you, “I will not leave you,” because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
You shall take an awl and pierce his ear at the threshold of the door, and he shall be your slave forever. You shall do the same with your female slave.

And do not consider it a hardship when you set them free from you, because year after year they have served you for six years at a hired worker’s wages. And the Lord your God will bless you in everything you do.
You shall consecrate to the Lord your God all the firstborn males born in your herd and your flock. You shall not put your firstborn ox to work, nor shear the firstborn of your flock.
Year by year you and your household shall eat it before the Lord in the place that the Lord your God chooses.
And if it has a defect, whether it is lame or blind or has any other serious defect, you shall not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
Instead, you shall eat it in your towns. The unclean and the clean among you may eat it alike, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
But you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it onto the ground like water.
Observe the month of the first crops and celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, for in the month of the first crops you came out of Egypt by night.
And you shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God, sheep and cattle, in the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be invoked there.

You must not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day of your departure from the land of the Egyptians all the days of your life.
No leaven shall be seen among you anywhere within your borders for seven days, and none of the meat that you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain overnight until morning.
You must not presume to sacrifice the Passover in any of your towns that the Lord your God gives you.
Rather, at the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called upon there, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at sunset, at the time when you left Egypt.
You shall cook and roast it and eat it at the place that the Lord your God chooses, and in the morning you shall return and go to your home.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a closing festival for the Lord your God. You must not do any work on it, except what is done for a person's needs.
You shall count seven weeks for yourself. From the time your sickle begins cutting the standing grain, you shall begin counting seven weeks.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks for the Lord your God, giving as much as your hand can provide, according to the means he gives you, in keeping with how the Lord your God blesses you.

You shall rejoice before the Lord your God—you, your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, the Levite who is in your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who are among you—at the place that the Lord God chooses for his name to be called upon there.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of the Egyptians, and you shall take care to carry out these commandments.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Booths for seven days, when you gather in the produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
You shall rejoice at your feast—you, your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who are in your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate a feast for the Lord your God at the place that the Lord your God chooses. And if the Lord your God blesses you in all your crops and in all the work of your hands, you shall be joyful.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God at the place the Lord chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty-handed.
Each person shall give according to the ability of his hands, according to the blessing that the Lord your God has given you.
You shall appoint judges and court clerks in all your towns that the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They must not show partiality or accept bribes, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and corrupts the words of the righteous.
You shall administer justice righteously, so that you may live and enter to inherit the land that the Lord God gives you.
You must not plant for yourself a grove of any kind of tree beside the altar of the Lord your God.
You must not make any votive object for yourself, and you must not set up for yourself a pillar, which the Lord your God hates.
You must not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has any blemish or any kind of defect, because that is an abomination before the Lord your God.
If there is found among you, in one of your towns that the Lord your God gives you, a man or woman who does evil before the Lord your God by transgressing his covenant,
and they go and serve other gods and bow down to them—to the sun or the moon or anything in the host of heaven—which I did not command,
and it is reported to you, you shall investigate thoroughly. If the report is indeed true and that abomination has been committed in Israel,
you shall bring that man or woman who committed the evil deed out to your gates, and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.
On the testimony of two or three witnesses, the person who is to die shall be put to death; no one shall be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to lay hands on him to kill him, and afterward all the people must do so. You shall remove the evil from among you.

If a matter of judgment in your towns is too difficult for you, involving one case of bloodshed and another, one legal claim and another, one injury and another, or one dispute and another, you shall rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be named there.
You shall go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who holds office in those days. They shall examine the matter and tell you the judgment.
You shall act according to the instruction given to you by those at the place the Lord your God chooses, and you shall be very careful to do everything as it is prescribed for you.
You shall act according to the laws and the judgment they tell you. Do not turn aside from what they tell you, either to the right or to the left.

Anyone who acts arrogantly, refusing to listen to the priest who stands to serve in the name of the Lord your God, or to the judge who holds office in those days, shall die. You shall remove the evil from Israel.
All the people shall hear and be afraid, and shall no longer act wickedly.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you, take possession of it, and live in it, and you say, “I will appoint a ruler over myself, like the other nations around me,”

you shall indeed appoint over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God chooses. You shall appoint a ruler from among your brothers. You may not appoint over yourself a foreigner who is not your brother.
He must not acquire many horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt, for the Lord said, “We must not return again by that same road.”
He must not take many wives for himself, lest his heart turn aside, nor accumulate excessive silver and gold for himself.
When he sits in his position of rule, you shall write for him in a book a copy of these laws, from the Levitical priests.
It shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord your God, to keep all these commandments, and to carry out these ordinances.

His heart must not become proud toward his brothers, and he must not turn aside from these commandments to the right or to the left, so that he and his sons may continue long in their rule among the Israelites.
The Levitical priests, the sons of Levi, shall have no share or inheritance with Israel. They shall eat the firstfruits of the Lord as their allotted portion.
They shall have no allotted portion among their brothers, for the Lord is their portion, as he told them.
These are the priest’s dues from the people who slaughter sacrificial animals: whether it is an ox or a sheep, they shall give the priest the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
You shall give them the firstfruits of your wheat, your wine, and your oil, and the first of the wool shorn from your sheep.
For the Lord chose him from all your tribes to stand before the Lord your God, to serve and to bless in his name, he and his sons for all time.
If a Levite comes from any of your towns among all the Israelites, where he has been living, and comes of his own desire to the place that the Lord chooses,
To serve the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord God.
He shall eat his allotted share, apart from what each receives from the sale of family property.
When you enter the land that the Lord God gives you, do not learn to act according to the abominations of those nations.
Let no one be found among you who makes his son or daughter pass through flame, practices divination, interprets omens, or reads omens from birds,
or casts spells, or is a medium or an interpreter of signs who consults the dead.
For everyone who does these things is abhorrent to the Lord, and because of such abominations the Lord will destroy them before you.
You shall be blameless before the Lord your God.
For those nations you are about to dispossess listen to soothsayers and diviners, but the Lord your God has not permitted you to do so.
The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.

This is in accordance with everything you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let us no longer hear the voice of the Lord our God or see this great fire, lest we die.”
And the Lord said to me, “Everything they have said is right.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will speak to them as I command him.
And if anyone does not listen to what the prophet speaks in my name, I will exact punishment from him.
But if a prophet presumptuously speaks anything in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or if he speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die.”
But if you say in your heart, “How shall we recognize a word that the Lord has not spoken?”
Whatever a prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come about or come true, that is a word the Lord has not spoken. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not spare him.
And when the Lord your God destroys the nations whose land the Lord your God gives you, and you take possession of it and live in their cities and houses,
you must set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of the land that the Lord your God gives you.
You must lay out the roads for yourself and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the Lord your God assigns to you, so that there may be a refuge there for anyone who kills someone.
This shall be the rule for anyone who kills someone and flees there to save his life: whoever strikes his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before,

or whoever goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, raises his hand with the axe to cut the wood, and the iron head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies—he shall flee to one of those cities and live.

Otherwise, the blood avenger might pursue the killer while his heart burns with anger, overtake him if the road is too long, and strike him dead, although he does not deserve a sentence of death, since he had not hated the man before.
Therefore I give you this command and say, “You must set apart three cities for yourself.”
And if the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as the Lord swore to your fathers, and the Lord gives you all the land he promised to give your fathers,
and if you obey and carry out all these commandments that I give you today, loving the Lord your God and walking in all his ways always, then you must add three more cities to those three.
Thus innocent blood shall not be shed in your land, which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, and no one among you shall be guilty of bloodshed.
But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises against him and strikes him dead, and then flees to one of those cities,
the elders of his city must send for him, take him from there, and hand him over to the blood avenger, and he must die.
You must show him no pity. You must remove the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, and it will go well with you.
You must not move your neighbor’s boundary markers, which your fathers established, in the inheritance you will possess in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.

A single witness shall not be sufficient to testify against a person concerning any wrongdoing, any offense, or any sin that he commits. Every matter shall be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If a false witness comes forward against a person and maliciously accuses him of some wicked act,
the two men who have the dispute shall stand before the Lord, before the priests, and before the judges who are serving in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly. If the witness proves to be unjust, having given false testimony and having stood against his brother,
you shall do to him as he intended to harm his neighbor. Remove the evil from among you.
The others shall hear and be struck with fear, and they shall no longer do such an evil thing among you.
Your eye shall have no pity on him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

If you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, horsemen, and a people more numerous than you, do not fear them, for the Lord your God is with you, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians.
When you approach the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
He shall say to them, “Listen, Israel! Today you are advancing into battle against your enemies. Do not let your hearts fail. Do not be afraid, do not be terrified, and do not flee from them,
for the Lord our God goes before you and with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.”
The officers shall speak to the people and say, “If anyone has built a new house and has not dedicated it, let him go back to his house, lest he die in battle and another man dedicate it.
If anyone has planted a vineyard and has not enjoyed it, let him go back to his house, lest he die in battle and another man enjoy it.”
Any man who has become engaged to a woman but has not married her shall go back to his house, lest he die in battle and another man marry her.
The officers shall continue speaking to the people and say, “If anyone is afraid and fainthearted, let him go back to his house, so that he does not make his brother’s heart fearful like his own.”
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of the army to lead the people.
If you approach a city to fight against it, offer its people peace.
If they give a peaceful answer and open the city to you, all the people found in it shall pay tribute and be subject to you.
But if they will not submit to you and make war against you, you shall besiege it.
