The Lord your God shall deliver it into your hands, and you shall strike down all its males with the sword,

except for the women, the furnishings, and all the livestock. Everything found in the city and all its goods you shall take for yourself as plunder. You shall eat all the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God gives you.
You shall do the same to all the cities that are very far away from you and are not cities of these nations.
But in the cities of these nations whose land the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, you shall not leave alive anything that breathes,
Instead, you shall utterly devote them to destruction—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—as the Lord your God commanded.
so that they do not teach you to practice all the abominations they performed for their gods, and you sin before the Lord your God.

If you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it to take it, do not destroy its trees by wielding an iron tool against them. You may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down. Is a tree planted in the field a human being, that it should come under siege before you?
But a tree that you know does not bear fruit you shall cut down and cut up, and build siegeworks around the city that wages war against you, until it is captured.
If someone is found slain in the land that the Lord your God gives you to inherit, lying in a field, and no one knows who struck him down,
your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distances to the cities around the slain person.
The elders of the city nearest to the slain person shall take a heifer from the herd that has not been put to work and has not borne a yoke.
The elders of the people shall bring the heifer down into a rocky valley that has not been cultivated or sown, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley.

The Levitical priests shall approach, because the Lord your God has chosen them to stand before him and to bless in his name, and every dispute and every assault shall be settled according to their word.
All the elders of the city nearest to the slain person shall wash their hands over the head of the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
They shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
Atone for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, Lord, so that innocent blood may not come upon your people Israel.” And the guilt of the blood shall be removed from them.
And you shall remove innocent blood from among you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
If you go out to war against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands, and you take captives from them,
and you see among the captives a woman of beautiful appearance, and desire her and take her as your wife,
you shall bring her into your house, shave her head, and trim her nails.

You shall remove the clothing she wore as a captive, and she shall remain in your house and mourn her father and mother for a month. Afterward you shall go in to her and live with her, and she shall be your wife.
If you are not pleased with her, you shall let her go free. You shall not sell her for money or treat her with contempt, because you have humiliated her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both the loved and the hated wife bear him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the hated wife,

then, on the day when he gives his possessions to his sons as an inheritance, he shall not be allowed to make the son of the loved wife the firstborn, disregarding the firstborn son of the hated wife.

Instead, he shall acknowledge the unloved woman's firstborn by giving him a double share of everything he possesses, because he is the first of his sons, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If someone has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father and mother, and they discipline him but he does not listen to them,
his father and mother shall seize him and bring him to the elders of their city, to the gate of their town.
They shall say to the men of their city, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious and does not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
The men of his city shall stone him to death. You shall remove the evil from among you, and the others shall hear and be afraid.
If someone is guilty of an offense punishable by death and is put to death, you shall hang him on a tree.

His body shall not remain overnight on the tree, but you shall surely bury him that same day, because everyone who hangs on a tree is cursed by God. You shall not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.
If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying on the road, you shall not ignore them, but shall surely turn them back and bring them to your brother.
But if your brother is not near you, or you do not know him, you shall gather them into your house, and they shall remain with you until your brother looks for them. Then you shall give them to him.
You shall do the same with his donkey, and the same with his clothing. You shall also do the same with anything your brother loses that you find. You shall not be allowed to ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road, you shall not pass them by. Instead, you shall help him raise them up.
Women must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing, for everyone who does this is detestable to the Lord your God.

If you come upon a bird's nest along your way, either in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs, and the mother is sitting over the chicks or eggs to keep them warm, you must not take the mother along with her young.
You must let the mother go, but you may take the young for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may live long on the earth.
If you build a new house, make a parapet around its roof, so that you do not bring bloodshed upon your house if someone falls from it.
Do not sow your vineyard with different kinds of seed, lest the crops and the seed you sow, together with the produce of your vineyard, become consecrated.
Do not plow with a donkey and an ox together.
Do not wear clothing made of wool and linen mixed together.
Make tassels of twisted cord on the four corners of the clothing you wear.
If a man takes a wife, marries her, and comes to hate her,
and brings slanderous accusations against her, gives her a bad name, and says, “I took this woman as my wife, but when I approached her, I found no evidence of her virginity,”
then the girl's father and mother shall take the evidence of the girl's virginity and bring it to the council of elders at the gate.
The girl's father shall say to the elders, “I gave this daughter of mine to this man as his wife, and he has come to hate her.”

“He brings slanderous accusations against her and says, ‘I found no evidence of your daughter's virginity.’ But here is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.” And they shall spread out the garment before the elders of that city.
The council of elders of that city shall take that man and discipline him.

They shall fine him a hundred shekels and give them to the girl's father, because he has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She shall remain his wife, and he shall not be allowed to divorce her for as long as he lives.
But if the accusation is true and no evidence of the girl's virginity is found,

they shall bring the girl to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has committed a disgraceful act among the children of Israel by prostituting herself in her father's house. You shall remove the evil from among you.
If a man is found committing adultery with a married woman, you shall put both of them to death—the man who committed adultery with the woman, and the woman. You shall remove the evil from Israel.
If a virgin girl is betrothed to a man, and another man finds her in the city and sleeps with her,

you shall bring both of them to the gate of their city and stone them to death—the girl because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. You shall remove the evil from among you.
But if a man finds a girl betrothed to a man in the countryside and forcibly sleeps with her, you shall put to death the man who slept with her.
Do nothing to the girl, for the girl has committed no offense deserving death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and kills him.
For he found her in the open country, and the betrothed girl cried out, but there was no one to help her.
If a man finds a virgin girl who is not betrothed to a man and forcibly sleeps with her,
the man who slept with her shall give the girl's father fifty silver double-drachmas. She shall become his wife, and he shall not be allowed to divorce her for as long as he lives.
A man must not take his father's wife or uncover his father's nakedness.
No man whose testicles are crushed or whose penis is cut off shall enter the assembly of God.
No child born of prostitution shall enter the assembly of the Lord.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the Lord. Even to the tenth generation they shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, nor shall they ever enter.
For they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia to curse you.
But the Lord your God would not listen to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into blessings, because the Lord your God loved you.
You shall not speak peaceably with them all your days, forever.
Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, for you were a foreigner in his land.
If they have children, those of the third generation may enter the assembly of the Lord.
When you go out to war and encamp against your enemies, guard yourself against every evil thing.
If there is a man among you who is not clean because of a nighttime emission, he shall go outside the camp and shall not enter the camp.
Toward evening he shall wash his body with water, and at sunset he may enter the camp.
You shall have a designated place outside the camp, and you shall go out there.
You shall have a peg on your belt, and when you squat outside, you shall dig with it and then cover your excrement.

For the Lord your God walks through your camp to save you and deliver your enemies into your hands. Your camp shall be holy, so that no filthy thing is seen among you and he does not turn away from you.
Do not hand over to his master a slave who comes to you from his master.
He shall live with you and settle among you in whatever place pleases him, and you shall not oppress him.

There shall be no female prostitute among the daughters of Israel and no male prostitute among the sons of Israel. There shall be no consecrated woman among the daughters of Israel and no dedicated man among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring a prostitute's wages or the price of a dog into the house of your God for any vow, for both are abominations before the Lord your God.
Do not lend your brother silver at interest, or food at usury, or at a percentage.
You may lend anything to a foreigner and to your brother, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land you are about to enter and possess.
If you make a vow to the Lord your God, do not delay fulfilling it, for the Lord your God will surely require it of you, and it will count as a sin against you.
But if you do not wish to make a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Be careful to carry out whatever passes your lips, just as you vowed to your God—the gifts you promised with your own mouth.
If you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat grapes until you are satisfied, but you shall not put any in a container.
If you enter your neighbor’s grain field, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hands, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor’s standing crop.

If a man takes a wife and goes in to her, and she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found something shameful in her, he shall write her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hands, and send her out of his house.
And if she goes to another man.
And if the latter husband hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hands, and sends her away from his house, or if her latter husband, who took her as his wife, dies,

her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back as his wife after she has been defiled, for that is defilement before the Lord your God. Do not defile the land that the Lord God will give you as an inheritance.
If a man has newly taken a wife, he must not go to war, nor must any other duty be imposed on him. He must be free of obligations at home and make happy the wife he has taken.
Do not take either the upper or the lower millstone as a pledge, for anyone who does so takes a life as a pledge.
If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers from among the children of Israel, mistreating him and selling him, the kidnapper must die. You must remove the evil from among you.
Guard yourself against the affliction of leprosy. Take care to act according to all the law that the Levitical priests explain to you, just as I commanded you to take care to do.
Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the journey when you came out of Egypt.
If your neighbor owes you any debt, do not enter his house to take anything as a pledge.
Instead, stand outside, and the man who owes you the debt must bring your pledge outside.
If the man is poor, his pledge must not remain overnight.
You must return his pledge at sunset, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you. This will count as an act of mercy for you before the Lord your God.
Do not withhold the wages of a poor and needy person, whether one of your brothers or one of the foreigners living in your towns.
Pay him his wages that same day, and do not let the sun set on them, because he is poor and they are his hope. Otherwise he may cry out against you to the Lord, and this will become a sin for you.
Fathers must not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers. Each person must be put to death for his own sin.
Do not pervert the justice due to the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and do not take a widow’s clothing as a pledge.
For you were a slave in the land of the Egyptians, and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do these things.

When you reap the harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in your field, do not go back to take it. It must be left for the poor, the foreigner, the widow, and the orphan, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you harvest olives, you shall not go back to gather the fruit left behind. It shall be for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
When you harvest your vineyard, do not glean what is left behind you. It must be left for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you too were a slave in the land of the Egyptians. That is why I command you to do these things.
If there is a dispute between people, they shall come before the court and be judged. The judges shall acquit the righteous and condemn the wicked.
If the guilty man deserves a beating, they must make him sit before the judges and strike him in their presence according to his wrongdoing,
with forty blows, and they must not add any more. If they add more blows than that, your brother will be degraded in your sight.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together and one of them dies without offspring, the dead man’s wife must not marry an outsider who is not related to him. Instead, her husband’s brother must go in to her, take her as his wife, and live with her.
The child who is born shall be established in the name of the deceased, so that his name may not be erased from Israel.
But if the man does not wish to take his brother’s wife, the woman must go to the gate, to the elders, and say, “My husband’s brother is unwilling to preserve his brother’s name among Israel.”
The elders of his town must summon him and speak with him. If he stands firm and says, “I do not wish to take her,”

Then his brother’s wife shall come forward before the elders, remove one sandal from his foot, spit in his face, and say, “This is what shall be done to the man who does not build up his brother’s house.”
And his name in Israel shall be “The house of the barefoot man.”

If men fight with one another, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them comes forward to rescue her husband from the hands of the man who is striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his testicles,
You shall cut off her hand, and your eye shall have no pity on her.
You shall not have in your bag two different weights, a large one and a small one.
You shall not have two measures in your house, a large one or a small one.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, so that you may live long in the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.
For everyone who does this, and everyone who acts unjustly, is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt:
how he met you on the way and cut off those at your rear, the exhausted people behind you, while you were hungry and weary; and he did not fear God.

When the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the Lord your God will allot to you as an inheritance, you shall erase the name of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance, take possession of it, and live in it,
you shall take the first of the fruits of your land that the Lord your God will give you, put them in a basket, and go to the place that the Lord God will choose for his name to be called upon there.
You shall go to the priest who serves in those days and say to him, “Today I give thanks to the Lord my God, because I have entered the land that the Lord swore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket from your hands and place it before the altar of the Lord your God.

Then you shall say before the Lord your God, “My father left Syria and went down to Egypt. He lived there as a foreigner, with few in number, and there he became a great nation and increased very, very greatly.
The Egyptians tormented us, mistreated us, and imposed harsh labor on us.
We cried out to the God of our fathers, and the Lord heard our voice and saw our suffering, our toil, and our oppression.
The Lord himself brought us out of Egypt with great power, a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, great visions, signs, and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
And now, behold, I bring the firstfruits of the produce of the land that the Lord gave me, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall bow down there before the Lord your God.
There you shall rejoice in all the good things that the Lord your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the foreigner living among you.

When you finish tithing all the tithes of your land in the second year, you shall tithe again for the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, and they shall eat in your towns and be satisfied.

You shall say before the Lord your God, “I have removed the holy things from my house and given them to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, according to all the commandments of the Lord God that he commanded me. I have not transgressed your commandment or forgotten it.
I have not eaten any of them while in mourning, nor offered any of them to the unclean, nor given any of them to the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God and done as you commanded me.
Now look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land that you gave them, as you swore to our fathers to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.”
On this day the Lord your God commanded you to carry out all these statutes and judgments. You shall keep them and carry them out with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today choose the Lord your God to be your God. You shall walk in his ways, keep his statutes and judgments, and listen to his voice.
And today the Lord chose you to be his own people, as he told you, and to keep all his commandments.
And you are to be above all the nations, as he made you renowned, prosperous, and glorious, and to be a holy people to the Lord your God, as he told you.
Moses and the elders of Israel gave this command, saying, “Keep all the commandments that I command you today.
On the day when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, you shall set up large stones there and coat them with plaster.

You shall write on the stones all the words of this law when you cross the Jordan, at the time when you enter the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, will give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, promised to give you.
When you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, as I command you today, on Mount Ebal and coat them with plaster.
You shall build an altar there to the Lord your God, an altar of stones, and no iron shall touch them.
You shall build the altar of the Lord your God with whole stones and offer burnt offerings on it to the Lord your God.
And there you shall offer a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord your God, and you shall eat and be satisfied there and rejoice before the Lord your God.
You shall write all these laws on the stones very clearly.”
Moses, the priests, and the Levites spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silent and listen, Israel! On this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.
You shall listen to the voice of the Lord your God and carry out all his commandments and statutes that I command you today.”
On that day Moses commanded the people, saying:
“These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you cross the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
The Levites shall respond and say in a loud voice to all Israel:
‘Cursed be the man who makes a carved or cast image, the handiwork of a craftsman, for it is an abomination to the Lord, and sets it up in secret.’ And the people shall respond and say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who dishonors his father or his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who moves his neighbor’s boundary markers.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who perverts justice for the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who leads a blind person astray from the road.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s nakedness.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with any animal.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
‘Cursed be anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she is his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ And all the people shall say, ‘So be it.’
Cursed is anyone who strikes his neighbor treacherously. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
Cursed is anyone who does not uphold all the words of these laws by carrying them out. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”

And if you faithfully listen to the voice of the Lord our God, taking care to carry out all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you and reach you if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the field.
The children of your womb will be blessed, as will the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Your storehouses and your granaries will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you go out and when you come in.
The Lord your God will deliver your enemies and your adversaries over to you, crushed before you. They will come against you by one road and flee from you by seven roads.
The Lord will send a blessing upon you in your storehouses and in everything you undertake in the land that the Lord your God will give you.
The Lord your God will establish you as his holy people, as he swore to your ancestors, if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and walk in his ways.
All the nations of the earth will see that the Lord’s name is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.

The Lord your God will make you abound in good things—in the children of your womb, the produce of your land, and the offspring of your livestock—in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give you, for as long as the heavens are above the earth.

The Lord will open for you the treasures of his goodness, the heavens, to give rain to your land at the proper time and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

You will rule over many nations, and they will not rule over you. The Lord your God will establish you as the head and not the tail; you will be above and not below, if you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today to keep and carry out.
You must not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, either to the right or to the left, to follow foreign gods and worship them.
But if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and carrying out all his commandments that I command you today, these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the field.
Your storehouses and your granaries will be cursed.
The children of your womb will be cursed, as will the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.

The Lord will send you decline, deprivation, and loss in everything you undertake and whatever you do, until the Lord destroys you, until he makes you perish swiftly because of the wickedness of your ways, because you have abandoned me.
The Lord will kindle death within you until the Lord destroys you from the land that you are entering to possess.
The Lord will strike you with distress, fever, chills, sharp pains, fear, scorching wind, and pallor. They will pursue you until they destroy you.
The heavens above your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you will be iron.
The Lord will make the rain of your land dust, and dirt will come down from heaven upon you until he has wiped you out and destroyed you.

The Lord will give you over to defeat before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee from them by seven roads, and you will be scattered throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead bodies will become food for the birds of heaven and the wild animals of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.
The Lord will strike you with the boils of the Egyptians, with hemorrhoids, with severe scabs, and with itching, so that you cannot be healed.
The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind.
You will grope at midday as a blind person gropes in darkness, and you will not make your ways straight. Then you will be oppressed and robbed all your days, and there will be no one to help you.
You shall take a wife, but another man shall take her away from you. You shall build a house, but you shall not live in it. You shall plant a vineyard, but you shall not harvest its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before you, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be seized from you and will not return to you. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and there will be no one to help you.
Your sons and daughters will be handed over to a foreign nation, and your eyes will strain as they look toward them, but your hand will be unable to reach them.
A nation you do not know will eat the produce of your land and all the fruits of your labor, and you will be oppressed and crushed all your days.
You will be driven mad by the sights your eyes will see.
The Lord will strike you with terrible boils on your knees and legs, from the soles of your feet to your head, and you will be unable to be healed.
The Lord will take you and the rulers you set over yourself to a nation that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will worship foreign gods made of wood and stone.
You will become a mockery, a spectacle, and a byword among all the nations to which the Lord takes you.
You will sow much seed in the field but gather little, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will not drink wine or take pleasure in it, because worms will eat it.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, because your olive trees will shed their fruit.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
Caterpillars will strike all your planted trees and the produce of your land.
The foreigner living among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you will sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until they have wiped you out and destroyed you, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God by keeping his commandments and statutes, which he commanded you.
And they shall be signs and wonders upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a sincere heart, despite your abundance of everything.
You will serve your enemies, whom the Lord will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has wiped you out.
He will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, swooping like an eagle—a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation with a fierce face, which will show no regard for the elderly and no mercy to the young.
And it will eat the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land, and it will leave you no grain, wine, or oil, no herds of cattle or flocks of sheep, until it has destroyed you.

And it will besiege you in all your cities until your high and fortified walls, in which you trusted throughout your land, have fallen. And it will besiege you in all your cities that the Lord your God gave you.
And you will eat the offspring of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the Lord gave you, in the distress and hardship with which your enemy will oppress you.
The tender and very delicate man among you will look with hostility at his brother, at the wife of his embrace, and at the children he still has left.

to give any one of them some of the flesh of his children, which he will eat because nothing is left to him in your distress and in the hardship with which your enemies will afflict you in all your cities.

And the tender and very delicate woman among you, whose foot has never ventured to walk on the ground because of her delicacy and tenderness, will look with hostility at the husband of her embrace, at her son, and at her daughter.

And she will roast and eat some of the afterbirth that comes out from within her and of the children she bears. Because she lacks everything, she will hide it, in the distress and hardship with which the enemy will oppress you in all your cities.
And if you do not obey and carry out all the words of this law written in this book, fearing the honored and wondrous name of the Lord your God,
the Lord will make the plagues upon you and your descendants extraordinary: great and astonishing plagues, and terrible and grievous illnesses.
And he shall bring upon you all the grievous diseases of the Egyptians, which you dreaded, and they shall lodge in you.
And the Lord shall bring upon you every illness and every affliction written in the book of these laws, until he destroys you.
And you will be left few in number, although you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.

And just as the Lord rejoiced over you in doing you good and multiplying you, so the Lord will rejoice over you in destroying you. And you will be uprooted from the land that you are entering to possess.
And the Lord your God will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve foreign gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers knew.
Even among those nations he will give you no rest, and there will be no resting place for the soles of your feet. There he will give you a sorrowful heart, failing eyes, and a wasted soul.
And your life will hang before your eyes, and you will be terrified night and day and have no confidence in your life.
In the morning you will say, “When will evening come?” And in the evening you will say, “When will morning come?” because of the terror you feel in your heart and the sights your eyes will see.

And the Lord will bring you back to Egypt in ships, with troops numbering in the thousands, and by that same road we shall not see it again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no one to buy you.
These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to establish with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant he made with them at Horeb.
And Moses called all the children of Israel and said to them, “You yourselves see everything that the Lord did in Egypt before you to Pharaoh, to his servants, and to his entire land:
the great trials that your eyes saw, those signs and great wonders, the mighty hand and the outstretched arm.
Yet the Lord your God has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day.
And he led you through the wilderness for forty years. Your clothes did not grow old, and the shoes on your feet did not wear out.
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.
And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us in battle.
And we struck them down and took their land, and I gave it as an inheritance to Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.
And be careful to carry out all the words of this covenant, so that you may understand everything you do.
Here you all stand today before the Lord your God: your tribal leaders, your elders, your judges, your scribes, and every man of Israel,
and your wives and your children, and the foreigner within your camp, from your woodcutter to your water carrier,
so that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into its curses, which the Lord your God establishes with you today,
so that he may establish you as his people and be your God, as he said and as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And it is not with you alone that I establish this covenant and these curses.
but also with those who are here with us today before the Lord our God, and with those who are not with us today.
For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of the Egyptians and how we passed among the nations through which you passed.
And you saw their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, which they possess.

Let there be no man or woman, family or tribe among you whose heart has turned away from the Lord our God to go and worship the gods of those nations. Let there be no root among you springing up in bitterness and harshness.
And if someone hears the words of these curses and thinks in his heart, saying, “May I be forgiven even if I walk according to the error of my heart,” let the sinner not destroy the innocent.

And God will not be willing to forgive him. Rather, his anger and his jealousy will then flare up against that man, and all the curses of this covenant written in this book of the law will come upon him, and the Lord will erase his name from under heaven.
And the Lord will single him out for calamity from all the children of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.

And the next generation and your children who arise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will speak when they see the plagues of that land and its afflictions which the Lord sent upon it:

the sulfur and salt burned throughout all its soil. Let it not be sown, let nothing sprout, and let no green plant grow upon it, as Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim were overthrown, which the Lord overthrew in wrath and anger.
And all the nations will say, “Why did the Lord do this to that land? What is the meaning of this great, fierce anger?”
They will answer and say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the God of their fathers, which he made with their fathers when he brought them out of the land of the Egyptians,
and they went and worshiped foreign gods and bowed down to them, gods whom they did not know and whom he had not allotted to them.
And the Lord became fiercely angry with that land, bringing upon it all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
And the Lord uprooted them from their land in anger and wrath and exceedingly great fury, and cast them into a foreign land, where they remain to this day.”
The hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things belong to us and our children forever, so that we may carry out all the words of this law.
And when all these declarations come upon you, whether blessings or curses, which I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where the Lord will scatter you,
and you return to the Lord your God and obey his voice according to everything I command you today, with all your heart and with all your soul,
And the Lord will heal your sins and have mercy on you, and will gather you again from all the nations among which the Lord scattered you.
Even if you are scattered from one end of the earth to the other, from there the Lord your God will gather you, and from there the Lord your God will bring you back.
And the Lord your God will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will possess it. It will go well with you, and he will make you more numerous than your fathers.
And the Lord will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and so that you and your offspring may live.
And the Lord your God will put these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.
And you will return and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and carry out his commandments which I command you today.

And the Lord your God will make you prosper in all the work of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, the produce of your land, and the offspring of your livestock. For the Lord your God will again rejoice over you in doing you good, just as he rejoiced over your fathers,

if you obey the voice of the Lord your God by keeping and carrying out all his commandments, his ordinances, and his judgments written in this book of the law, and if you return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For this commandment which I command you today is not too burdensome, nor is it far from you.
It is not in heaven, so that you should say, “Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it, so that we may hear it and carry it out?”
Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you should say, “Who will cross beyond the sea and bring it to us and make us hear it, so that we may carry it out?”
The word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, and it is in your hands to carry it out.
See, today I have set before you life and death, good and evil.

And if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you today—to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his ordinances, his commandments, and his judgments—you will live and become numerous, and the Lord your God will bless you throughout the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns away and you do not obey, and you are led astray and bow down to foreign gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you will utterly perish, and you will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.
Today I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life, so that you and your offspring may live,

loving the Lord your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him. For this is your life and the length of your days, so that you may dwell in the land which the Lord swore to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And Moses finished speaking all these words to all the children of Israel.
And he said to them, “I am one hundred and twenty years old today, and I can no longer go out and come in, for the Lord said to me, ‘You will not cross this Jordan.’
The Lord your God goes before you. He will destroy those nations before you, and you will take possession of them. And Joshua goes before you, as the Lord has said.
And the Lord will do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, and to their land, just as you destroyed them.
And the Lord will deliver them before you, and you will deal with them as I commanded you.
Be courageous and strong. Do not fear, hesitate, or be terrified before them, for the Lord your God himself will go ahead of you and be among you. He will not abandon you or cast you down.

Moses called Joshua and said to him before all Israel, “Be courageous and strong, for you will enter at the head of this people into the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them, and you will cause them to inherit it.”
“The Lord who will go with you will not abandon you or cast you down. Do not fear or hesitate.”
Moses wrote all the words of this law in a book and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and to the elders of the children of Israel.
Moses commanded them that day, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, at the Feast of Tabernacles,
when all Israel gathers to appear before the Lord your God at the place the Lord chooses, we shall read this law before Israel, in their hearing.
Gather the people—men, women, children, and the foreigner who is in your towns—so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord our God and learn to carry out all the commands of this law.
Their children, who do not know it, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord our God all the days they live on the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, the days of your death are approaching. Call Joshua, and stand before the entrance of the tent of testimony, and I will give him instructions.” Moses and Joshua went to the tent of testimony and stood at its entrance.
The Lord descended in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, you will sleep with your fathers, and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves by following the foreign gods of the land they are entering, among its people. They will abandon me and break my covenant that I made with them.

I will be fiercely angry with them on that day. I will abandon them and turn my face away from them, and they will become food for their enemies. Many evils and afflictions will come upon them, and on that day they will say, ‘These evils have come upon us because the Lord our God is not with us.’
I will certainly turn my face away from them on that day because of all the evils they have done, for they have turned to foreign gods.
Now write down the words of this song of praise, teach it to the children of Israel, and put it in their mouths, so that this song of praise may be a testimony for me among the children of Israel.

For I shall bring them into the good land that I swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey. They shall eat and be filled and satisfied, and they shall turn to foreign gods and serve them. They shall provoke me to anger and break the covenant that I made with them.

This song of praise will stand against them as a witness, and it shall not be forgotten from their mouths or from the mouths of their descendants. For I know the evil they have done here today, before I have brought them into the good land that I swore to their fathers.”
Moses wrote this song of praise that day and taught it to the children of Israel.
Moses commanded Joshua son of Nun, saying, “Be courageous and strong, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land that the Lord promised to give them, and he will be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, to the very end,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, saying:
Take this book of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and let it remain there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebelliousness and your stubbornness. Even today, while I am still alive among you, you provoke God. How much more will you do so after my death!
Now gather to me your tribal chiefs, your elders, your judges, and your court scribes, so that I may speak all these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth as witnesses against you.

For I know that after my death you will act utterly lawlessly and turn aside from the way I commanded you. Evils will befall you in the last days, because you will do evil before the Lord, provoking him to anger by the works of your hands.
And Moses spoke the words of this blessing in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel, right to the end.
Pay attention, heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my speech be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew, like rain upon the grass and like a downpour upon the vegetation.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord. Give praise to the Lord our God.
God, whose works are true and all whose ways are just, is a faithful God, and there is no injustice in him. The Lord is righteous and blameless.
They sinned, and not against him—blemished children, a crooked and perverse generation.
Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not the Father who acquired you, made you, and established you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years from generation to generation. Ask your fathers, and they will tell you; ask your elders, and they will speak to you.
When the Most High divided all the nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he established the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the sons of God.
The Lord’s portion became his own people, Jacob; Israel was his allotted inheritance.
He provided for him in the wilderness, in scorching thirst, in a waterless land. He protected him, instructed him, and guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle covering its nest, he had compassion on his young. He spread his wings, received him, and lifted him up and carried him on his back.
The Lord alone led them, and no foreign god was with them.
He brought them up to the riches of the land and fed them with the produce of the fields. He gave them honey to suck from the rock and oil from the flinty rock.
Butter from cows and milk from ewes, together with the fat of lambs and rams, young bulls and male goats, with the rich kernels of wheat; and they drank the blood of grapes as wine.
Jacob ate and was satisfied; he grew strong, and the beloved one kicked. He grew fat, thick, and broad, and abandoned the Lord God, his Maker, and rebelled against God his Savior.
They provoked me to anger with foreign things, and embittered me with their abominations.
They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods they did not know, new ones that had recently come, whom your fathers did not know.
You abandoned God who begot you; you forgot God who nourished you.
The Lord saw and became jealous, and was enraged by the provocation of his sons and daughters.
And he said, “I will turn my face away from them and show them what will happen in the last days, for they are a perverse generation, children in whom there is no faithfulness.

They made me jealous with things that are not gods and provoked me to anger with their idols. And I will make them jealous with those who are not a nation, and provoke them to anger with a foolish people.
For a fire has been kindled by my anger. It will burn down to the lowest depths of hell, consume the earth and its produce, and set the foundations of the mountains ablaze.
I will heap evils upon them and spend my arrows against them.
Wasted by hunger and devoured by birds, with incurable spasms; I will send the teeth of wild beasts against them, to drag them across the earth in fury.
Outside the sword will bereave them, and terror from the storehouses will strike the young man together with the virgin, the nursing child together with the man of advanced age.
I said, [?], “I will scatter them; I will make their memory cease among humankind,”
were it not for the anger of their enemies, lest they live long, and lest their adversaries exalt themselves and say, “Our hand is mighty, and it was not the Lord who did all this.”
For they are a nation that has lost its judgment, and there is no wisdom in them.
They did not consider understanding this; now let them receive it in times to come.
How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless God had sold them?
For their gods are not like our God, and our enemies are foolish in their counsel.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, and their branch from Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall, and their cluster is bitterness.
Their wine is the venom of dragons and the incurable venom of vipers.
Is not all this gathered with me and kept sealed in my treasury?
On the day of vengeance I will repay them, at the time when their foot slips, for the day of their destruction is near, and what has been prepared is at hand for you.
For the Lord will judge his people and have compassion on his servants, because he saw them weakened, abandoned, and handed over into captivity.
And the Lord said, “Where are their gods, in whom they had placed their hope,
whose sacrificial fat you ate and whose wine offerings you drank? Let them rise and help you, and let them be your support.
See, see that I am he, and there is no other besides me. I kill, and I give life; I strike, and I heal, and there is no one who can deliver from my hands.
For I will raise my hand to heaven and swear by my right hand, and I will say, ‘I live forever.’
For I will sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand will take hold of judgment. I will repay my enemies with vengeance, and I will repay those who hate me.

I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh—from the blood of the wounded and the captives, from the heads of the enemy’s rulers.” Rejoice, heavens, together with him, and let all the sons of God worship him.

Rejoice, nations, with his people, and let all the angels of God strengthen him, for he avenges the blood of his sons. He will exact vengeance and execute judgment upon his enemies, and he will repay those who hate him; and the Lord will cleanse the land of his people. And Moses wrote this song of praise on that day and taught it to the children of Israel.
And Moses came among the people and spoke all the words of these laws in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
And Moses finished speaking to all Israel,
and said to them, “Pay careful attention in your hearts to all these words that I testify to you today. You must command your children to keep and carry out all the words of these laws.
For this is not an empty word for you, because it is your life, and through this word you will live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses that same day and said:
Go up to Mount Abarim, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land that I will give the children of Israel as a possession.
And die there on the mountain that you ascend, and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
because you rebelled against my word among the children of Israel at the waters of Strife at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not show my holiness among the children of Israel.
You shall see the land before you, but you shall not enter it.
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death.
And he said: The Lord will come from Sinai, and he appeared to us from Seir, and he hastened from Mount Paran with ten thousands at Kadesh; at his right hand his angels were with him.
And he spared his people, and all the holy ones are under your hand, and they are with you.
And he received from his words the law that Moses commanded us, the inheritance of the assembly of Jacob.
And there shall be a ruler among the beloved one, when the rulers of the peoples are assembled together with the tribes of Israel.
May Reuben live and not die, and may he be numerous.
And he said this about Judah: Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and come to his people; may his hands decide for him, and may you be his helper against his enemies.
And about Levi he said: Give Levi his revelation and his truth, to the blameless man whom they tested with trials and accused at the waters of Strife,
who said to his father and his mother, ‘I have not seen you,’ and did not acknowledge his brothers and did not recognize his sons. He was attentive to your words and kept your covenant.
They shall declare your judgments to Jacob and your law to Israel; they shall place incense in your wrath, continually upon your altar.
Bless his strength, Lord, and accept the works of his hands. Crush the loins of his enemies who rise against him, and let those who hate him not stand.
And about Benjamin he said: The one beloved by the Lord shall dwell in confidence, and God shall be a shelter for him all his days, and he rested between his shoulders.
And about Joseph he said: His land is under the Lord’s blessing, from the seasons of heaven and from the dew and from the deep springs below,
from the seasonal produce of the sun’s changing course, and from the gathering of clouds together,
from the summits of the ancient mountains and from the tops of the everlasting hills.
and according to the seasonal fullness of the earth. And may the favors of the one who appeared in the bush come upon Joseph’s head and upon the crown of the one glorified among his brothers.

His beauty is that of a firstborn bull, and his horns are the horns of a unicorn. With them he shall gore the nations together, as far as the ends of the earth. These are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.
And about Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out. And about Issachar he said: In their dwellings nations shall be destroyed,
and you shall summon them there and offer a righteous sacrifice, for he will nourish you with the abundance of the sea and the profits of merchants living by the seashore.
And about Gad he said: Blessed is the one who enlarged Gad. He rested like a lion and crushed arms and rulers.

And he saw his dominion, for there the land of rulers was divided with the peoples, together with the heads of the nations, the tribes of Israel. He carried out the Lord’s righteousness and his judgment with Israel.
And of Dan he says: Dan is a lion’s cub and will spring out of Bashan.
And of Naphtali he says: Naphtali is satisfied with favor and will be filled with blessing from the Lord; he will inherit the sea and the south.
And of Asher he says: Blessed among sons is Asher. Let him be welcomed by his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
And his shoes will be iron and bronze. As your days are, so will your strength be.
There is none like the God of the beloved, who ascends to heaven as your helper and is majestic in the firmament.
And there is shelter in God’s dominion and in the strength of everlasting arms. He will drive the enemy away from before you and will say, “Perish!”
And Israel will dwell securely, alone in the land of Jacob, amid grain and wine; and the heavens will be a storehouse of dew for him.
Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people chosen by the Lord? Your helper will protect you, and the sword is your boast. Your enemies will come, and you will climb upon their necks.
And Moses went up from Araboth of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Peor, which is opposite Jericho. And the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead as far as Dan,
and all the land of Naphtali, and all the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the farthest sea,
and the wilderness and the region around Jericho, and the cities of palm trees as far as Zoar.
And the Lord said to Moses: “This is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have shown it to your eyes, but you shall not enter it.”
And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab according to the word of the Lord.
And they buried him in Gai, near Beth-peor, and no one has known his grave to this day.
And Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyes had not grown weak, and his cheeks had not become wrinkled.
And the children of Israel wept for Moses in Araboth of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, for thirty days. And the days of mourning and weeping for Moses came to an end.
And Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hand upon him. And the children of Israel obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And no prophet arose again in Israel like Moses, a man whom the Lord knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders that the Lord sent him to perform in the land of the Egyptians against Pharaoh and his servants and all his land,
the great signs, the mighty hand, and the uplifted arm that Moses displayed before the children of Israel.
